reason: Cooling the lava and rock directly addresses the goal of making the surface able to retain liquid water.
expectation: I expect the surface to lose heat and produce cooler rock, though it may need further cooling.

alternatives.reason: Cool air could help make rain, but I want to cool the surface first so water can stay.

effect: The cool rock can retain liquid water, so the remaining goal is to make rain.
reaction: The contrast between cool rock and nearby lava makes the uneven cooling clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should advance the rain goal.
expectation: I expect water vapor to condense in the cooler air, perhaps forming clouds or rain.

effect: Condensation formed clouds; the remaining step is to bring their water to the ground.
reaction: The distinction between clouds and a surface sea is useful.
reason: This is the only offered combination and should produce rain.
expectation: I expect gravity to bring water from the clouds down as rain.

effect: Rain is falling, but some can evaporate or boil, so I should direct it onto cool rock.
reaction: The possibility of rain evaporating before reaching the ground adds a useful complication.
reason: Cool rock can retain liquid water, unlike the nearby lava.
expectation: I expect some rain to reach the cool rock and remain liquid, though some may evaporate on the way.

alternatives.reason: Rain on hot lava could show the contrasting boiling process, but it seems less useful for retaining water.

effect: Rain remains liquid on cool rock, completing the chapter and making accumulation possible.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the earlier cooling choice pay off.

mostWorthwhile.text: Cooling the surface and then directing rain onto it made the conditions for liquid water clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making clouds and then rain felt fairly predictable, especially with only one combination offered each time.

surprise.text: Rain could evaporate in hot air or boil on lava even while nearby cool rock could retain it.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the offered combinations had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to see how retained rain accumulates into a sea; the contrast between neighboring hot and cool surfaces was engaging.
